title: Restock for the Festive Rush
summary: Aunty Zainab can only afford to restock three fabrics. Find the three that bring in the most money.

client.name: Aunty Zainab
brief: Festive season is coming and everybody wants new clothes for owambe. But my money can only restock three fabrics.
My apprentice says Brocade because we sell the most yards. I'm not sure. Which three bring in the most money?
client.thanks: Chiffon! My apprentice will hear it today. Come back for owambe season, I'll sew you something fine.

starterSql:
-- Zee Fabrics: which three fabrics bring in the most money?
-- Careful: wholesale buyers pay less per yard than retail customers.

SELECT *
FROM sales
LIMIT 20;

tables.name: sales
tables.description: Zee Fabrics sales book, 10–13 November. Prices change from sale to sale: wholesale buyers get a big discount.

columns.name: price_per_yard
columns.desc: Price charged per yard on this sale, in naira (₦)

hints.title: Hint 1: Yards aren't money
hints.desc: A fabric can sell lots of yards cheaply. Money from a sale is yards × the price on that sale.

hints.title: Hint 2: Multiply before you add
hints.desc: Work out each sale's money first, then add per fabric. Averaging the price per yard gives the wrong answer when prices vary.

hints.title: Hint 3: Keep the top three
hints.desc: GROUP BY fabric, sort by revenue from highest to lowest, LIMIT 3. Return the fabric and its revenue.

findings.claim: Which fabric should she restock first?

options.text: Brocade: it sells the most yards
Chiffon: it brings in the most money
Swiss lace: it's the most expensive

findings.claim: Why was the apprentice's advice misleading?

options.text: Brocade moves lots of yards, but mostly to wholesale buyers at a steep discount.
It wasn't. Brocade earns the most.

successFeedback: Chiffon earns the most even though Brocade sells more yards: Brocade's big wholesale orders go at a steep discount. Volume isn't value.

fixtures.purpose: The sales book you can see
fixtures.failHint: Your top three fabrics or their revenue don’t match the sales book.

fixtures.purpose: A week with deep wholesale discounts
fixtures.failHint: Revenue must use each sale’s own price. Multiply yards by price_per_yard on every row before adding.
Your query gives the wrong top three on a different week of data.
